data.gender_notes: Marguerite is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from 'Margarita', a form of 'Mary' in Latin, meaning 'pearl'. Used as a name for Mary in the Middle Ages. The name Marguerite carries the meaning “Mary's pearl” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Marguerite usually hope their child will grow to embody mary's pearl and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Marguerite total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_hebrew.name: מרגרט
in_hebrew.long_meaning: מרגרט הוא שם שמקורו בפרסית ופירושו פנינה יקרה ויפהפייה. השם עבר דרך היוונית והלטינית והפך לשם נוצרי פופולרי. ביהדות, הפנינה היא סמל ליופי וערך פנימי.

in_greek.name: Μαργαρίτης
in_greek.long_meaning: Ο όρος Μαργαρίτης προέρχεται από το λατινικό Margarita, το οποίο με τη σειρά του προέρχεται από το ελληνικό μαργαρίτης, που σημαίνει πολύτιμος λίθος. Ο όρος συσχετίζεται με την έννοια του μαργαρίτη ως σύμβολο πνευματικής αγνότητας και ομορφιάς.

in_latin.name: Margarita
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Margarita derivatum est ex latino Margarita, quod Graecum μαργαρίτης, significat pretiosus lapis. In ecclesia primitiva, margarita symbolum erat puritatis et pulchritudinis spiritualis.

in_english.name: Marguerite
in_english.long_meaning: The name Marguerite originates from the Persian word for pearl, which was adopted into Greek as μαργαρίτης (margaritēs) and then into Latin as Margarita. It symbolizes purity, beauty, and spiritual richness. Historically, the name gained popularity in Christian tradition due to its association with the pearl of great price mentioned in the New Testament (Matthew 13:45-46). The pearl is a symbol of spiritual wealth and enlightenment.

data.cultural_impact: The name 'Marguerite' has a rich cultural history, particularly in Europe. It has been used as a personal name since the Middle Aages, and was often given to girls born on the feast day of St. Margaret, a popular saint in the Christian tradition. Marguerite is also the name of several notable historical figures, including Queen Marguerite of France and Marguerite de Navarre, a writer and patron of the arts.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Marguerite holds a deep spiritual significance as a form of Mary, the mother of Jesus. In Christianity, Mary is highly revered as a model of faith, obedience, and devotion. The name Marguerite serves as a reminder of the preciousness and worth of each individual as a unique and valuable pearl in the eyes of God. Additionally, flowers named after the saint, such as the Marguerite daisy, have become symbols of purity and devotion.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Marguerite: Daisy of the Lord. A name evoking purity, devotion, and the blossoming of the soul in faith.
